name: @helm/desktop
description: Helm's Electron shell: main process, preload, renderer.
//productName: Electron derives app.getName() - and therefore %APPDATA%\<name> - from this file. Without productName a scoped package name puts the database in %APPDATA%\@helm/desktop, creating a nested folder from the scope. electron-builder sets the same value for packaged builds.
author: Cole Taylor

scripts.//dev: Goes through scripts/run-dev.mjs, which gives the run a data directory of its own under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Helm\dev and points it at a synthetic gh. Without that, productName: Helm resolves userData to %APPDATA%\Helm - the installed app's - and the two fight over one Chromium profile and one helm.db. --fresh starts with no database, which is the first-run state. A second `pnpm dev` gets its own directory rather than failing on a held helm.db.
scripts.//dev:live: The old behaviour: unpackaged, against %APPDATA%\Helm, sharing everything with the installed app. Kept because it is the only way to see the real database and the real gh in a dev build, and it says so loudly on the console and on the status bar's mode chip. --watch is what makes the main process and preload reload too; without it electron-vite only gives the renderer HMR, and every main-process edit needs the app killed and restarted by hand.
scripts.//fidelity: TUI fidelity inside xterm - C1 to C9, against the spike page rather than the app. Goes through run-isolated.mjs like every other check: without it, productName: Helm resolves userData to %APPDATA%\Helm, so the run shared a Chromium profile with the installed app somebody is working in and wrote its report and its nine screenshots into that app's data directory. --fresh because this page opens no database at all, so seeding a VACUUM INTO copy of the real one would be work with no reader. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network, but it does drive the real clipboard: C5 and C7 write to it and leave it empty. Pass --only=C1,...,C9 to re-run one check.
scripts.//claude-check: Deliberately still unwrapped, and the only check left that is - it is out of scope for the change that isolated fidelity, not a decision that it does not need the same treatment. It resolves userData to %APPDATA%\Helm exactly as fidelity did.
scripts.//design-shot: Not a check. Opens the real window, walks the main views, and screenshots each in both themes - evidence for a design review against docs/DESIGN.md. Four groups, narrowed with --only=views,states,responsive,split (the GROUPS const in src/main/designshot.ts is the authority): views is the walk, states the collapsed section, responsive the width sweep over the two scoped headers - which prints each header's overflow and spill rather than only photographing it - and split the docked pane, which is the one that spawns a real claude session and the only one that reaches pane widths below the window's own minWidth.
scripts.//affordance-check: Does everything clickable look clickable. Walks the seven main views in the real window, enumerates every button, link, select, tab and checkbox on each, and puts a real pointer on each one in turn - asserting it computes cursor: pointer and that some computed property actually changes underneath it. Three named hover probes live in design-shot and cannot answer 'all', which is what the Tailwind '@media (hover: hover)' failure was. Two controls are planted first, one that must be flagged and one that must pass, because an auditor is not believed until it has been made to fail. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network; about a minute and a half. Pass --only=cursor|hover|quiet to re-run one group.
scripts.//highlight-check: The editors: the overlay under the textarea, the highlighting over debounced IPC, and the editing behaviour. Drives the real window against a fixture harness the driver owns and never clicks Save - HL-16 hashes the fixture tree either side and requires it unchanged, because this milestone touches the one surface in Helm that writes into a .claude tree. Three things in it are worth knowing. The scroll claim is made twice, in two currencies: the transform the component wrote and the rectangle the browser actually put the underlay at. The parity comparator is made to fail first - a font size is forced onto one layer and the same function has to reject the pair it just accepted, and the trailing-newline half switches off the pseudo-element that materialises the last line and requires the heights to stop matching. And latency is measured in frames rather than milliseconds, because 'inside one frame' is a discrete claim: an input listener the driver installs counts requestAnimationFrame callbacks to the first one where the underlay shows what the textarea holds, and anything but 1 is a frame the character was not on screen for. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network; about two minutes. Pass --only=edit|parity|behaviour|latency|degrade|theme to re-run one group.
scripts.//sessions-check: Session lifecycle - launching, tabs and teardown - driven through the real app window. Spawns real claude sessions and ends them; see src/main/sessionscheck.ts.
scripts.//profiles-check: Profiles and overlay composition. Builds a profile through the real form, launches it, and asks the live session whether the composition worked. Three phases, orchestrated by run-profiles.mjs rather than by && because node-pty's teardown loses the exit code; the report is the verdict. Pass --only=form|compose|fixture|shims through to re-run one group; form spawns no session.
scripts.//history-check: The session index and resume. Drives the session-history pane through the real window and checks every count against an independent read of ~/.claude/history.jsonl. Spawns two real claude sessions - one resumed through the app, one on its own pty to prove the index notices a session Helm did not start - so it takes minutes. Verdict is in history-report.json; run-history.mjs exists for the same reason run-profiles.mjs does.
scripts.//config-check: The config console. Drives it through the real window: browses every scope against an independent readdir walk, edits a file in each and restores it hash-verified, adds an MCP server through the UI, then launches a real claude session and asks it whether the effective view predicted what it actually sees. Spawns one claude session on haiku, so it takes minutes. Pass --only=browse|edit|snapshot|json|external|mcp|effective|doctor to re-run one group.
scripts.//content-check: The content viewer. Opens every markdown file in the user's harness vault through the real window and checks the DOM it produced against a regex read of the same source, navigates a wikilink, interrogates the artifact frame's sandbox from inside it, measures search latency and scroll frame intervals, and edits a real note through the split editor with a hash-verified restore. Spawns no claude sessions, so it takes about a minute. Pass --only=browse|render|links|artifact|search|edit|scroll to re-run one group.
scripts.//packaging-check: Packaging, first run and the personal-path audit, in three phases. Phase 1 audits this checkout for personal paths (having first planted one to prove the auditor catches it) and checks the CLI Helm would launch against an independent 'where.exe' read. Phase 2 is a second app started with PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR pointed at a temp directory - the app's own portable-mode mechanism used as isolation - so first run happens against an empty database and an absent .claude without touching the real ones: it adds plain folders, scaffolds a harness and launches a real session from it, exercises the repos: key, converts a folder in place, and points the version guard at a stub CLI reporting 9.9.9. Phase 3 builds the artefacts if they are missing and runs the portable exe from a path with spaces. It does NOT install anything: verifying the NSIS installer means removing the Helm on this machine, so that is a tool (verify:installer) and not a group here, and PKG-2 stands open in the report to say so. Pass --only=audit|cli|firstrun|harness|scan|version|package to re-run one group.
scripts.//verify:installer: DESTRUCTIVE, and run by name only. Installs the built NSIS package over the Helm installed on this machine, runs its selftest, and uninstalls it - leaving no installed Helm behind. Refuses without --yes, and refuses again if Helm is running unless --replace-running. Not reachable from any suite: Helm hosts Claude Code sessions, so ending it ends the work inside it.
scripts.//usage-check: The status bar's usage figures. Drives the real window: checks the painted percentages against its own JSON.parse of ~/.claude.json, watches a rewritten fixture reach the bar with no restart, lets a usage window roll over underneath the segment, points the reader at six broken readings and proves each paints nothing, measures the bar at four widths in both themes, measures the full transcript parse it avoids, asks a live claude for /usage and compares, and finally gives the reader two installs' `.claude.json` at once and proves the freshest reading wins with nothing merged. The report lands in helm-data/usage-report.json under the check's own data directory. Pass --only=<groups> to re-run one group; the group list is the GROUPS const in src/main/usagecheck.ts, which is the only authority for it.
scripts.//settings-check: The settings pane and every app setting. Drives it through the real window: opens it from the title bar gear, points the CLI setting at a stub program and clears it again, adds two scan roots and removes one - checking the removal against the next scan's project set rather than against the list - flips the theme and reads back the colour Electron was handed for the window controls, sets the usage mode and confirms it on the status bar, clicks both quick accessors and watches the pane follow, and hand-sends a malformed write for every key after proving a valid one lands. Every UI assertion sits beside this driver's own read-only connection to the database file. Two phases, orchestrated by run-settings.mjs: the driver parks the settings it changed and a second app start reads them back and restores the originals. The terminal group spawns one claude session and nothing else does: the font and cursor claims are about live terminals in both registries, and only a session puts one in the session registry. The github group points ghPath at a gh that is installed and not signed in, which is the only honest way to see the 'run gh auth login' sentence on a machine whose real gh is signed in, and sets the polling interval through the pane including the 0 that disarms the timer. Pass --only=pane|claude|roots|appearance|accessors|validation|terminal|github|wsl to re-run one group. The `wsl` group writes no settings row at all - it drives the `.wslconfig` control against a fixture profile reached by swapping `USERPROFILE`, which is why it runs last, and it opens the restart dialog and cancels rather than confirming it.
scripts.//pr-check: The pull-request surface: fetch, cache, detail tab, review launch and degradation. Four of its five phases answer from a gh this repo wrote - scripts/fake-gh.mjs behind a .cmd shim, aimed at the service with pointGh - because a pull request whose title changes between two passes, an authentication that fails and a payload that is not JSON are not things a real repository can be made to do on demand. The fixture is mutated underneath the same comparison before its clean pass is believed. Beside every claim about the pane there is a read the driver makes for itself: its own JSON.parse of the fixture, its own read-only connection to helm.db, its own git and its own gh. The review phase spawns real claude sessions and closes them; the checkout phase runs a real gh pr checkout in a real git repository in a path with a space and reads the branch back out of git. The live phase runs the real gh once against a repository it found by walking the scan roots itself, and skips out loud when the machine has no gh, no sign-in or nothing open. It borrows the real database and puts the settings back; run-prcheck.mjs restores them too if the driver dies first. Pass --only=fixture|detail|review|degrade|live to re-run one group.
scripts.//transcript-check: The transcript archive: capture, the byte cursor, full-text search over archived messages, the storage ceiling and its eviction rule, and the read-only guarantee over Claude Code's own tree. Runs against a .claude tree of the runner's own, pointed at with the real CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR rather than a flag - so honouring that variable is something the run exercises rather than something a hook simulates. Two phases, orchestrated by run-transcript.mjs: phase one archives a conversation and records it, the runner deletes the transcript, and a second real app start has to find the conversation still readable and still searchable. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network; about a minute and a half, most of it spent waiting for the watch to notice a planted transcript on its own. Pass --only=setup|capture|incremental|search|bounded|readonly to re-run one group.
scripts.//browser-check: The integrated browser pane, driven through the real window in two phases. The driver starts its own HTTP and HTTPS fixture servers on 127.0.0.1 - a known title, a background colour that appears nowhere in theme.css, a console.log token, and a self-signed certificate it mints at run time rather than committing a private key or depending on openssl - so a run spawns no claude sessions and touches no network. Three shapes in it are worth knowing. BR-3 pins the milestone spike as a permanent assertion: with the tab not showing, capturePage has to return a frame painted a colour the page had never been before it was hidden, executeJavaScript has to answer, and a synthesised click has to reach the document - which is what M17 is built on and would otherwise regress with nothing on screen looking different. Every claim that the view is hidden is settled by counting the fixture colour in a capture of the window rather than by asking Helm what it last told Electron, and BR-5 runs that counter over a shown frame and a hidden one first, because a counter stuck at zero would pass every hiding probe. And the second app start exists because a cookie surviving a restart is not a claim the process that stored it can make; the fixture rebinds the port phase one wrote down, since an origin includes the port. About two minutes. Pass --only=pane|wins|bounds|hidden|console|reach|isolation|postures|persist|intact to re-run one group.
scripts.//template-check: Harness templates: the engine, the picker, and the seeding. Five app starts, orchestrated by run-template.mjs. Three of them are windowless `--template-seed` starts, because "a first start seeds the directory", "a second overwrites nothing" and "deleting it re-seeds" are claims about startup that no started process can make about itself; the runner edits a seeded file between two of them, since Helm keeps no hashes and so cannot tell an edited file from an untouched one. The fourth start drives the real New Harness dialog: it picks a planted fixture template out of the real picker, creates, and then walks the result with a recursion that knows nothing about templates - the dot-claude alias, the .gitkeep folder, the .tpl that lost its extension, and a workflow file full of literal {{...}} that has to arrive byte-identical, which is what says substitution stayed inside .tpl. That byte comparator is made to fail on a mutated fixture before its clean answer is believed. The hostile group refuses four template names that are paths, through the real channel, and drives a template carrying a Windows junction: the honest half is written, the junction is a sentence, and what it pointed at is hashed either side. Spawns no claude sessions and touches no network; about a minute. Pass --only=create|minimal-unchanged|seed|hostile to re-run one group.
scripts.//dist:win: Goes through scripts/dist-win.mjs rather than calling electron-builder directly. electron-builder resolves pnpm with which(), which prefers pnpm.EXE over pnpm.CMD on Windows; a stale standalone pnpm shadowing the managed one makes it either fail outright or - worse - fall back to the npm collector and silently produce artefacts with no app.asar.unpacked, which is an exe that cannot dlopen better-sqlite3. The wrapper checks the resolved pnpm answers the declared version and shims it for the child process if not.
scripts.//verify:artifact: Asserts a built exe actually carries app.asar.unpacked, by unwrapping the NSIS artefact and the app-64.7z nested inside it. Checking dist-app/win-unpacked instead would be checking electron-builder's scratch directory rather than the file a person downloads. With no arguments it checks every Helm-*.exe in dist-app; the release workflow names the two it is about to upload. Needs 7-Zip, which ships on the windows-latest runner image.
scripts.//icon: Draws build/icon.* and packs build/icon.ico. The .ico is committed, so this is not part of the build - run it when the artwork changes.

//electron: Pinned exactly, not a range. electron-builder downloads platform binaries for one specific release and refuses to guess which - a caret here fails the packaging step outright (electron-builder 26.15.3). It is also the right shape regardless: the packaged app must ship the runtime the drivers measured against.
